content_html:
Existentialism: From 20th‑Century Movement to 21st‑Century Continuum

Existentialism is historically linked to the early–mid 20th century (Kierkegaard & Nietzsche as precursors; Heidegger; Sartre; de Beauvoir; Camus; Merleau‑Ponty). Yet its core questions - freedom, authenticity, responsibility, meaning amid uncertainty - remain structurally active today across philosophy, psychology, environmental humanities, and technology ethics.

Then → Now

20th‑century focus 21st‑century continuity (2019–2025)
Being, temporality, thrownness (Heidegger) Renewed work in phenomenology & embodiment; temporality of self across contexts
Freedom, bad faith, project (Sartre) Meaning‑making and agency in clinical & positive psychology (PP 2.0); values‑based living
Embodiment & perception (Merleau‑Ponty) Embodied/4E cognition reviews (2023–2025) link phenomenology and cognitive science
Absurdity & revolt (Camus) Eco‑anxiety & Anthropocene meaning; public‑facing medicine & humanities essays
Authenticity, ethics, relation (de Beauvoir) AI value alignment debates using phenomenology; responsibility in design
Existential risk (term broadened) Policy & public discourse on extinction‑level risks (AI, bio, climate)
